memory_update.text: SPSC should be the primary underfollowed candidate for the retail supplier network node; verify recurring revenue mix, trading-partner count, net retention/churn, and retailer-specific integration evidence in filings.

OTEX and DSGX are broader B2B/logistics network operators with plausible but less pure exposure to retail supplier EDI and compliance plumbing; require vertical revenue segmentation before prioritization.

ETWO/e2open would have been a relevant public candidate for retail/supply-chain network software, but it was acquired by WiseTech Global and delisted from NYSE in 2025, removing it from the US-listed universe.

Private or no-longer-public assets such as Rithum/CommerceHub/ChannelAdvisor and 1WorldSync appear highly relevant to product catalog, dropship, and marketplace supplier connectivity but are not current US-listed candidates; use them as private comps or customer-workflow maps.

Avery Dennison may be an adjacent physical-to-digital compliance and item-level data capture provider through RFID, variable data management, and atma.io, but it is not a pure EDI/order-management network candidate and should be tested in a separate retail compliance / product identity pass.

node: Retail supplier networks, EDI, order-management, catalog, compliance, and replenishment plumbing
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow but investable US-listed universe around retail trading-partner connectivity. The strongest underfollowed chokepoint candidate is SPS Commerce, whose retail/supplier network appears directly aligned with embedded EDI, order, invoice, compliance, and retailer-specific workflows. OpenText and Descartes provide broader B2B / logistics networks that can serve as reference or secondary exposure, but retail purity needs segmentation work. Manhattan Associates is a higher-attention reference name for order-management and supply-chain execution rather than a scarce EDI network. Avery Dennison is noted in memory as a possible adjacent physical-to-digital compliance input, but excluded from the candidate list to keep this pass focused on software/network plumbing.
